title: Geodesic (the 'pure math spine') depends on the scene graph via snap_candidate
evidence:
scripts/geodesic.gd:4-7
## Pure great-circle math on a sphere (E1.1 surface-math core).
## Convention: points are world-space positions relative to the planet CENTER.
## Surface points have length == planet radius. All functions are static and
## side-effect free so the headless suite can verify every contract.

scripts/geodesic.gd:102
static func snap_candidate(point: Vector3, candidates: Array, snap_arc: float) -> Node3D:

scripts/geodesic.gd:108
		var arc := arc_angle(point, (n as Node3D).global_position)

 corroborating: tests/test_geodesic.gd:89-98 must stage real Node3D into tree.root to test this 'pure' module:
	var near_node := Node3D.new()
	tree.root.add_child(near_node)
	near_node.global_position = Vector3(R * cos(0.08), R * sin(0.08), 0)
detail: The module's own contract declares pure, static, scene-free math, yet snap_candidate consumes Node3D world transforms. E2's deterministic sim builds on this spine; the math-to-scene dependency direction is backwards.
recommended_fix: Accept plain Vector3 positions (parallel candidates array or Callable) and resolve NodeSite in ConnectController; keep Geodesic free of scene-tree types.

scripts/connect_controller.gd:124-126 — the projection the game actually runs:
## Ray-cast the planet collider (physics layer 1) — physics so props/ocean behave

detail: Epic story E1.1 lists 'surface projection' as contract math; the analytic implementation ships nowhere — the verb uses physics ray-casts. Contract tests validate dead code while gameplay runs different code.
recommended_fix: Either route _project_pointer through ray_sphere (analytic planet-centered sphere, no physics dependency) or delete ray_sphere and pin the projection contract on the physics path.

title: ZOOM_STOPS hardcodes distances tuned to R=8, ignoring WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS
detail: Camera ladder distances are absolute literals tied to R=8 only by comment; every other module reads WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS. A radius retune (already happened once per spec change log) silently desyncs framing.
recommended_fix: Derive ZOOM_STOPS from WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS (e.g. [2.75, 1.94, 1.44] × R) so the single radius constant remains the source of truth.

title: Epic test contracts are white-box: assertions on underscore-private members across modules
evidence:
scripts/orbit_camera.gd:78-79 (docstring says Public, name says private):
## Public + pure so the headless suite can sweep it for the no-roll contract.
func _apply_pose(azimuth: float, latitude: float, distance: float) -> void:

tests/test_gesture.gd:45
	check(controller._source == a, "press on a node enters the DRAW state")
tests/test_gesture.gd:49
	check(controller._snap_target == b, "pointer over B snaps to B (arc-intent)")
tests/test_no_sim.gd:97
	check(arc._radius_scale > 1.0, "merged bundle renders fatter")
tests/test_camera.gd:57
	check(approx(_rig._target_distance, 15.5), "ladder step in -> district stop")
detail: The suite is the spec-of-record acceptance criteria, yet it asserts _source/_snap_target/_radius_scale/_target_distance/_mode internals. Benign internal refactors break the contract suite while behavior still holds.
recommended_fix: Drop the underscore on intended test seams (apply_pose); assert observable outcomes (pipe_count, registry size, preview visibility, camera_up) instead of raw private state.

title: Connection topology state lives in the input/view controller ahead of E2's sim
detail: The pair→count registry is network topology state owned by a scene-tree input controller. E2.1's sim core needs pooled capacity per pair, forcing later extraction or a sim→view dependency.
recommended_fix: When E2 lands, extract the registry into a sim-owned network model and keep ConnectController a thin presenter; note the intended seam in the spec now.
